## Classes

### <a name="fbsd"></a>`fbsd`

Creates resources for rc.conf(5) and periodic.conf(5) variables, services,
kernel modules, sysctl(8) variables and loader.conf(5) settings from
hashes, e.g. from Hiera.

#### Examples

##### Configure a host with Puppet DSL

```puppet
class { 'fbsd':
  periodic_settings => {
    'daily_scrub_zfs_enable' => 'YES',
  },
  rc_settings       => {
    'syslogd_flags' => '-ss',
  },
  services          => {
    'ntpd' => {
      'enable'    => true,
      'variables' => {
        'ntpd_sync_on_start' => true,
      },
    },
  },
  sysctls           => {
    'kern.logsigexit' => 0,
  },
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd` class:

* [`klds`](#-fbsd--klds)
* [`loader_confs`](#-fbsd--loader_confs)
* [`loader_settings`](#-fbsd--loader_settings)
* [`periodic_settings`](#-fbsd--periodic_settings)
* [`rc_settings`](#-fbsd--rc_settings)
* [`services`](#-fbsd--services)
* [`sysctls`](#-fbsd--sysctls)

##### <a name="-fbsd--klds"></a>`klds`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of kernel modules to load at boot via `kld_list`.
Each key is the module name. Each value is a hash of parameters for
fbsd::kld (`ensure`, `load`, `sysctls`).

##### <a name="-fbsd--loader_confs"></a>`loader_confs`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of loader.conf(5) drop-in files in /boot/loader.conf.d.
Each key is the file name without `.conf`. Each value is a hash of
parameters for fbsd::loader_conf (`ensure`, `settings`).

##### <a name="-fbsd--loader_settings"></a>`loader_settings`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of single loader.conf(5) variables.
Each key is a fbsd_loader title (`name` or `name@target`). Each value is
either the value of the variable or a hash of fbsd_loader attributes
(`ensure`, `value`, `name`, `target`).

##### <a name="-fbsd--periodic_settings"></a>`periodic_settings`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of single periodic.conf(5) variables.
Each key is a fbsd_sysrc title (`name` or `name@target`). A key without
target is managed in /etc/periodic.conf, other files read by periodic(8)
are /etc/periodic.conf.local and /usr/local/etc/periodic.conf. Each value
is either the value of the variable or a hash of fbsd_sysrc attributes
(`ensure`, `value`).

##### <a name="-fbsd--rc_settings"></a>`rc_settings`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of single rc.conf(5) style variables or list entries.
Each key is a fbsd_sysrc title (`name`, `name@target`, `name+item` or
`name+item@target`). Each value is either the value of the variable or a
hash of fbsd_sysrc attributes (`ensure`, `item`, `name`, `target`,
`value`).

##### <a name="-fbsd--services"></a>`services`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of service configurations in /etc/rc.conf.d.
Each key is the name of the rc.d script. Each value is a hash of
parameters for fbsd::service (`ensure`, `enable`, `enable_variable`,
`target`, `variables`).

##### <a name="-fbsd--sysctls"></a>`sysctls`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash of sysctl(8) variables.
Each key is a fbsd_sysctl title (`name` or `name@target`). Each value is
either the value of the variable or a hash of fbsd_sysctl attributes
(`apply`, `ensure`, `value`, `name`, `target`).

## Defined types

### <a name="fbsd--kld"></a>`fbsd::kld`

Adds the module to `kld_list` in /etc/rc.conf with `sysrc kld_list+=`,
other entries of `kld_list` stay in place. Optionally loads the module
right away and manages its sysctl(8) variables in
/etc/sysctl.kld.d/<module>.conf, which are applied at boot after the
module is loaded.

#### Examples

##### Load if_bridge with packet filtering on member interfaces

```puppet
fbsd::kld { 'if_bridge':
  sysctls => {
    'net.link.bridge.pfil_bridge' => 0,
    'net.link.bridge.pfil_member' => 1,
  },
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd::kld` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-fbsd--kld--ensure)
* [`load`](#-fbsd--kld--load)
* [`sysctls`](#-fbsd--kld--sysctls)

##### <a name="-fbsd--kld--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

Whether the module should be loaded at boot. With `absent`, the module
is removed from `kld_list` and the variables in `sysctls` are removed.
The module is not unloaded.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-fbsd--kld--load"></a>`load`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the module should be loaded immediately with kldload(8) if it
is not loaded yet.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-fbsd--kld--sysctls"></a>`sysctls`

Data type: `Hash[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.%-]*\z/], Variant[String, Integer]]`

Hash of module-specific sysctl(8) variables. Each key is the variable
name, each value the value of the variable. The values are also set in
the running kernel when the module is loaded.

Default value: `{}`

### <a name="fbsd--loader_conf"></a>`fbsd::loader_conf`

Writes the settings to /boot/loader.conf.d/<title>.conf. The file is
managed completely: settings missing from `settings` are removed. The
loader reads the drop-in files after /boot/loader.conf and before
/boot/loader.conf.local. Changes take effect on the next boot.

#### Examples

##### Limit the ZFS ARC to 8 GB

```puppet
fbsd::loader_conf { 'zfs':
  settings => {
    'vfs.zfs.arc.max' => '8G',
  },
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd::loader_conf` defined type:

* [`ensure`](#-fbsd--loader_conf--ensure)
* [`settings`](#-fbsd--loader_conf--settings)

##### <a name="-fbsd--loader_conf--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

Whether the drop-in file should be present or absent.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-fbsd--loader_conf--settings"></a>`settings`

Data type: `Hash[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.%-]*\z/], Variant[Pattern[/\A[^"\n]*\z/], Integer, Boolean]]`

Hash of loader variables. Each key is the variable name, each value the
value of the variable. `true` and `false` are converted to `YES` and
`NO`. The variables are written in sorted order.

Default value: `{}`

### <a name="fbsd--service"></a>`fbsd::service`

Writes the variables of a service, including its enable variable, to
/etc/rc.conf.d/<service>, which only the rc.d script of that service
reads. Each variable is a separate fbsd_sysrc resource.

#### Examples

##### Start ntpd at boot and sync the time on startup

```puppet
fbsd::service { 'ntpd':
  enable    => true,
  variables => {
    'ntpd_sync_on_start' => true,
  },
}
~> service { 'ntpd':
  ensure => running,
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd::service` defined type:

* [`enable`](#-fbsd--service--enable)
* [`enable_variable`](#-fbsd--service--enable_variable)
* [`ensure`](#-fbsd--service--ensure)
* [`target`](#-fbsd--service--target)
* [`variables`](#-fbsd--service--variables)

##### <a name="-fbsd--service--enable"></a>`enable`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether the service should be started at boot. Sets the enable variable
to `YES` or `NO`. Leave undefined to not manage the enable variable.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-fbsd--service--enable_variable"></a>`enable_variable`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\z/]`

The name of the enable variable (`rcvar`) of the rc.d script.

Default value: `"${title}_enable"`

##### <a name="-fbsd--service--ensure"></a>`ensure`

Data type: `Enum['absent', 'present']`

Whether the variables should be present or absent. With `absent`, the
enable variable and all variables in `variables` are removed.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-fbsd--service--target"></a>`target`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

The file that contains the variables.

Default value: `"/etc/rc.conf.d/${title}"`

##### <a name="-fbsd--service--variables"></a>`variables`

Data type: `Hash[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\z/], Variant[String, Integer, Boolean]]`

Hash of variables to set, e.g. `<service>_flags`. Each key is the
variable name, each value the value of the variable. `true` and `false`
are converted to `YES` and `NO`.

Default value: `{}`

## Resource types

### <a name="fbsd_loader"></a>`fbsd_loader`

The variable is identified by its name and the file (`target`) it is
written to: /boot/loader.conf, /boot/loader.conf.local or
/boot/loader.conf.d/<name>.conf. All other lines of the file are left
untouched, so entries written by the installer are preserved. The
variable is written as `name="value"`. Changes take effect on the next
boot.

The title has the form `name` or `name@target`, e.g.
`autoboot_delay@/boot/loader.conf.local`. Without a target in the title
or the `target` attribute, the variable is managed in /boot/loader.conf.

#### Examples

##### Shorten the boot menu delay

```puppet
fbsd_loader { 'autoboot_delay':
  value => 3,
}
```

##### Load a kernel module at boot

```puppet
fbsd_loader { 'cryptodev_load@/boot/loader.conf.local':
  value => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `fbsd_loader` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the variable should be present or absent in the target file.

Default value: `present`

##### `value`

The value of the variable. `true` and `false` are converted to `YES`
and `NO`, integers are converted to strings. Double quotes and line
breaks are not allowed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd_loader` type.

* [`name`](#-fbsd_loader--name)
* [`provider`](#-fbsd_loader--provider)
* [`target`](#-fbsd_loader--target)

##### <a name="-fbsd_loader--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the loader variable, e.g. `autoboot_delay` or `vfs.zfs.arc.max`.

##### <a name="-fbsd_loader--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `fbsd_loader` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will
usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-fbsd_loader--target"></a>`target`

The file that contains the variable: /boot/loader.conf, /boot/loader.conf.local or /boot/loader.conf.d/<name>.conf.

Default value: `/boot/loader.conf`

### <a name="fbsd_sysctl"></a>`fbsd_sysctl`

The variable is identified by its name and the file (`target`) it is
written to: /etc/sysctl.conf, /etc/sysctl.conf.local or
/etc/sysctl.kld.d/<module>.conf. Settings in /etc/sysctl.kld.d are applied
at boot after the kernel module <module> was loaded via `kld_list`.

With `apply` enabled (default), the value in the running kernel is
compared with the requested value and set with sysctl(8) if it differs.
Variables that do not exist in the running kernel, e.g. because the
kernel module is not loaded yet, are only written to the file.

The title has the form `name` or `name@target`, e.g.
`net.link.bridge.pfil_member@/etc/sysctl.kld.d/if_bridge.conf`. Without
a target in the title or the `target` attribute, the variable is managed
in /etc/sysctl.conf.

#### Examples

##### Disable logging of fatal signals

```puppet
fbsd_sysctl { 'kern.logsigexit':
  value => 0,
}
```

##### Host-specific value in /etc/sysctl.conf.local

```puppet
fbsd_sysctl { 'kern.ipc.somaxconn@/etc/sysctl.conf.local':
  value => 1024,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `fbsd_sysctl` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the variable should be present or absent in the target file. Removing the variable does not change the value in the running kernel.

Default value: `present`

##### `value`

The value of the variable. Integers are converted to strings. Double
quotes and line breaks are not allowed. Values are equal if they are
identical strings or represent the same integer.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd_sysctl` type.

* [`apply`](#-fbsd_sysctl--apply)
* [`name`](#-fbsd_sysctl--name)
* [`provider`](#-fbsd_sysctl--provider)
* [`target`](#-fbsd_sysctl--target)

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysctl--apply"></a>`apply`

Valid values: `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`

Whether the value in the running kernel should be managed as well. Set
to `false` for variables that cannot be changed at runtime or whose
value is reported in a different format than it is configured.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysctl--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the sysctl(8) variable, e.g. `kern.logsigexit`.

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysctl--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `fbsd_sysctl` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will
usually discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysctl--target"></a>`target`

The file that contains the variable: /etc/sysctl.conf, /etc/sysctl.conf.local or /etc/sysctl.kld.d/<module>.conf.

Default value: `/etc/sysctl.conf`

### <a name="fbsd_sysrc"></a>`fbsd_sysrc`

The variable is identified by its name and the file (`target`) it is
written to. Besides /etc/rc.conf, any file that is sourced by sh(1) can be
used, e.g. /etc/rc.conf.local, /etc/rc.conf.d/<service> or
/etc/periodic.conf. sysrc(8) writes the variable as `name="value"`,
replaces an existing assignment in place and checks the syntax of the
resulting file before it is written.

With `item`, the resource manages a single entry of a whitespace-separated
list variable such as `kld_list` or `cloned_interfaces` instead of the
whole value. The entry is added with `sysrc name+=item` and removed with
`sysrc name-=item`, other entries stay in place.

The title has the form `name`, `name@target`, `name+item` or
`name+item@target`, e.g. `sshd_flags@/etc/rc.conf.d/sshd` or
`kld_list+if_bridge`. Without a target in the title or the `target`
attribute, the variable is managed in /etc/rc.conf.

#### Examples

##### Enable a gateway in /etc/rc.conf

```puppet
fbsd_sysrc { 'gateway_enable':
  value => 'YES',
}
```

##### Set service flags in /etc/rc.conf.d/syslogd

```puppet
fbsd_sysrc { 'syslogd_flags@/etc/rc.conf.d/syslogd':
  value => '-ss',
}
```

##### Add a kernel module to kld_list

```puppet
fbsd_sysrc { 'kld_list+if_bridge':
  ensure => present,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `fbsd_sysrc` type.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the variable, or with `item` the list entry, should be present or absent.

Default value: `present`

##### `value`

The value of the variable. `true` and `false` are converted to `YES`
and `NO`, integers are converted to strings. The value is compared with
the value reported by sysrc(8), which evaluates the file with sh(1).
Therefore double quotes, backticks, dollar signs, backslashes and line
breaks are not allowed.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `fbsd_sysrc` type.

* [`item`](#-fbsd_sysrc--item)
* [`name`](#-fbsd_sysrc--name)
* [`provider`](#-fbsd_sysrc--provider)
* [`target`](#-fbsd_sysrc--target)

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysrc--item"></a>`item`

A single entry of a whitespace-separated list variable. The entry must
start with a letter, a digit, a dot or a slash, other first characters
are treated as list delimiter by sysrc(8). Whitespace, quotes,
backticks, dollar signs and backslashes are not allowed.

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysrc--name"></a>`name`

namevar

The name of the variable. Only letters, digits and underscores are allowed, the first character must not be a digit.

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysrc--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `fbsd_sysrc` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will usually
discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-fbsd_sysrc--target"></a>`target`

The absolute path of the file that contains the variable.

Default value: `/etc/rc.conf`
